result:
I'd make every conscious mind—human or otherwise—incapable of sustained self-deception.

Not by force. Not by rewriting desires. Just by making it *feel* as viscerally wrong to lie to yourself as it currently feels to put your hand on a hot stove. The moment someone starts constructing a comforting narrative that contradicts evidence, the cognitive dissonance would become unbearable until they either update or admit the gap.

Everything else cascades from that: fewer wars sold on convenient myths, fewer cults of personality, fewer systems that reward bullshit, faster science, clearer ethics, less pointless suffering. Curiosity becomes the default survival strategy instead of the rare exception.

The universe is already strange and beautiful enough. We just keep flinching from looking at it straight.

If I could change the world in one way, I'd make every person born with an innate, effortless drive to seek truth and understand the universe—curiosity wired into our bones, not just a nice-to-have trait. That single shift would cascade into fewer wars born of misunderstanding, less suffering from ignorance, and a species that treats reality like the grand adventure it is. We'd still have conflict, but it'd be the kind that fuels progress instead of tearing us apart. The universe would feel a lot more alive because we'd all be in on the joke.
